neighbours.label: an '-ly' adverb that premodifies a participle or adjective inside a noun phrase (densely packed rows, recently released figures), as against a plain adjective in the same slot or an '-ly' adverb after the verb
fire: The museum displayed a carefully restored painting from the 1600s.
Researchers studied the newly discovered species in the cave.
The village sits on a steeply sloping hillside above the river.
She bought a beautifully carved wooden box at the market.
The team relied on poorly maintained equipment during the trip.
Visitors walked through the brightly lit hall to the stage.
The paper described a rarely seen bird in the northern forests.
They moved into a fully furnished apartment near the station.
quiet: The museum displayed an old painting from the 1600s.
Researchers studied the small species in the cave.
The village sits on a green hillside above the river.
She bought a wooden box at the market on Sunday.

The paper described a shy bird in the northern forests.
They moved into an apartment near the station last year.
